title: A regulator and the first market law
summary: Law 4628 created EPDK, the independent regulator, and set the first framework for a competitive electricity market. Per the handbook it split the state utility TEAŞ into separate generation (EÜAŞ), transmission (TEİAŞ) and wholesale companies, introduced the free consumer and foresaw a market financial settlement centre.

title: Reform strategy: privatise distribution first
summary: The March 2004 strategy paper set the order of the 2000s reform: privatise distribution first, then generation, create portfolio generation companies and replace cost-based tariffs with an equalisation mechanism. This is as TEPAV summarises it in a critical 2006 note; the paper itself was not read.

title: Renewable support law
summary: Law 5346 set purchase prices that licensed renewable plants in the support mechanism receive for ten years if commissioned between 18 May 2005 and 31 Dec 2020; for later plants the President sets prices. Law 6094 amended it in December 2010, and the handbook dates the start of the YEKDEM mechanism to 2011.

title: Provisional balancing and settlement begins
summary: Per the handbook, hourly load-up and load-down instructions were priced at the system marginal price (SMF) and settled monthly in three time zones. It was the first working balancing market, run by the settlement centre PMUM.

title: Nuclear sales law
summary: Law 5710 lets TETAŞ buy the electricity a nuclear plant is contracted to produce under a purchase contract of up to 15 years, and resell it to licensed companies in proportion to their share of national consumption.

title: Balancing and Settlement Regulation (DUY)
summary: The DUY, in force today in amended form, sets how balancing, the day-ahead and intraday markets, imbalance and financial settlement work. Many later market changes are amendments to it.

title: Day-ahead planning and hourly settlement
summary: Per the handbook, this was the first step towards a day-ahead market: settlement became hourly and consumers began to forecast their own consumption.

title: Trial parallel operation with continental Europe
summary: The Turkish grid was connected to the continental European system over two 400 kV lines to Bulgaria and one to Greece, for a one-year trial in three phases: stabilisation, non-commercial exchange and limited capacity allocation.

title: Day-ahead market opens (GÖP)
summary: The hourly day-ahead market that sets the PTF was established on 1 December 2011. The handbook dates the collateral and advance payment system to the same time.

title: The Electricity Market Law
summary: Law 6446 is the main law today. It defines the organised wholesale markets run by EPİAŞ, Borsa İstanbul and TEİAŞ and is the basis for EPİAŞ's organisation regulation; per the handbook it merged wholesale and retail licences into one supply licence. The Licence Regulation followed in November 2013.

title: Distribution privatisation completed
summary: A press report says the last sale completed the transfer of distribution to the private sector: 18 of 20 distribution companies were sold for about 12.7 billion USD, the other two handled separately by the Ministry.

title: Grid and cross-border trade rules
summary: Two regulations a few days apart set the technical rules for the transmission and distribution grids (Grid Regulation) and for cross-border electricity trade (Import and Export Regulation). The import and export rules were amended in 2014, 2019 and 2021.

title: EPİAŞ takes over the markets
summary: EPİAŞ took over the day-ahead and intraday markets and imbalance settlement from the earlier operator on 1 September 2015; TEİAŞ kept the balancing power market and holds a 49-year market operation licence of its own. The handbook dates the opening of the intraday market (GİP) to 1 July 2015.

title: TEİAŞ joins ENTSO-E as an observer
summary: TEİAŞ states it was the first and only observer member of ENTSO-E. This is why ENTSO-E data covers only Bulgaria, Greece and Georgia for Türkiye.

title: Transparency Platform launched
summary: Per the handbook, EPİAŞ's Transparency Platform opened in March 2016. It is the source of most data on this site.

title: Renewable resource areas (YEKA)
summary: Law 6719 added resource areas to the market law: the Ministry opens areas through competitive tenders, with guarantees and TEİAŞ connection opinions. The YEKA Regulation of October 2016 sets the competition as an open auction that starts from a price ceiling and runs down to the lowest price.

title: First 1,000 MW wind auction
summary: The winners were reported as Siemens Gamesa, Kalyon and Türkerler. One news summary gives a winning price of 3.48 against a ceiling of 7.00 without stating the unit (US cents per kWh assumed, not confirmed).

title: Ancillary services rules replaced
summary: The 2017 Ancillary Services Regulation replaced the 2008 text and is the base for the current rules, which TEİAŞ applies when procuring ancillary services. It was amended on 29 December 2025.

title: Capacity mechanism
summary: TEİAŞ proposes an annual budget that the EPDK board approves each November, paid to eligible plants by source type in proportion to installed capacity. Plants with YEKDEM support, wind and solar, plants with a public share above 50% and small plants are excluded.

title: Storage and demand response enter the market law
summary: Law 7103 added electricity storage and demand side participation to the activities listed in Article 14(1)(e) of the market law, within limits set by the board.

title: Unlicensed generation
summary: Renewable plants up to 1 MW, or the limit set by the President, need no licence and can offset their production against consumption in the same distribution region. The rules were amended in 2022 and 2023 and several times since.

title: Tariffs Regulation
summary: It defines the tariff types (connection, transmission, wholesale, distribution, retail, market operation and last resort supply) and the principles of revenue regulation.

title: Guarantee certificates for renewable electricity (YEK-G)
summary: The market operator issues certificates, one per MWh, as proof that supplied electricity came from renewable sources. The certificates can be traded.

title: Free consumer limit keeps falling
summary: Consumers above the limit can choose their supplier, so a lower limit widens the free market. The limit was cut to 1,200 kWh for 2021 (from 1,400) and to 500 kWh for 2026; a press report gives 750 kWh for 2025, down from 950.

title: Renewable support priced in lira
summary: Law 7257 (December 2020) moved the support charge to lira, and presidential decision 3453 set lira prices for plants commissioned from July 2021 to December 2025. A press report gives hydro 40, wind and solar 32 and geothermal 54 kuruş per kWh, with 8 kuruş for domestic equipment.

title: Import and export capacity rules
summary: The amendment limits exports by generation licensees to their installed capacity and sets how suppliers and generators bid for capacity on synchronous links, including guarantees, resale of transmission rights, loss of unused rights and the use of congestion revenue.

title: Storage Activities Regulation
summary: Four storage types are allowed: with a generation plant, with a consumption facility, standalone (supply licence holders, at least 2 MW) and built by network operators. Pumped hydro is excluded. Five other regulations were amended the same day to cover storage.

title: Power Futures Market opens (VEP)
summary: Law 7162 (January 2019) added forward physical delivery markets and EPİAŞ risk management, and EPDK decision 8965-2 set the operating procedures. Trading began on 1 June 2021, with a first reported trade at 405 lira per MWh for the October 2021 base contract; EPİAŞ acts as central counterparty.

title: Price caps on the day-ahead and balancing markets
summary: The earliest step in this site's price cap table is 2,500 TL/MWh from 1 April 2022 (earlier steps, if any, are not covered); the latest verified is 4,500 TL/MWh from 4 April 2026. EPDK lists the procedure the caps are set under beneath the DUY; its own text was not read.

title: Electric vehicle charging
summary: Charging network operators need an EPDK licence (up to 49 years, minimum capital 4.5 million TL), at least 50 units in at least 5 districts within 6 months, and fees that follow costs plus a reasonable margin, with EPDK able to set minimum and maximum prices.

title: Wind and solar pre-licences tied to storage
summary: Law 7417 lets companies that commit to build storage obtain a wind or solar pre-licence up to the storage capacity, exempt from the measurement and competition rules. Existing licensed plants may add capacity if they build storage, and the electricity can benefit from YEKDEM.

title: New intraday bid types
summary: From 1 January 2024 the intraday market has hourly contracts with partial amounts and new bid types (standard, time limited, fill or kill, fill and kill, price and time tiered, iceberg), with trades at the price of the bid entered first.

title: Aggregators
summary: The Aggregation Regulation (effective 1 January 2025) lets aggregators act for grid users that are not market participants. Law 7429 (December 2022) is where aggregation entered the market law, which is inferred from law-firm dates and not read. Per the handbook, the portfolio limit is 2,000 MW, of which unlicensed at most 500 MW.

title: Storage availability rules
summary: The January 2025 storage amendment added a definition of availability for storage in generation plants and a 10% tolerance at acceptance. Press reports on the wider package give 85% availability for five years and then 80%, and a plan for 15-minute balancing settlement by 1 January 2027. Per the handbook, the DUY amendment of the same day lets the board set the imbalance coefficients k and l.

title: Climate Law and the emissions trading system
summary: Law 7552 gives the Climate Change Presidency the job of setting up the emissions trading system and allocating allowances, and names EPİAŞ as market operator, running the market, financial settlement and the registry. The market manipulation fines of the Electricity Market Law extend to this market.

title: December 2025 package: storage, ancillary services, imbalance
summary: Storage is allowed at unlicensed plants under conditions and can take part in ancillary services and the balancing power market. Aggregators get rules for ancillary services. Per the handbook, from 1 January 2026 the imbalance coefficients depend on the system direction (k = 0.06 and l = 0.03 in a deficit, 0.03 and 0.06 in a surplus).

title: Tariff increase and a higher price cap
summary: A press report says residential tariffs rose 25% from 4 April 2026, low-voltage public services 17.5% and medium-voltage industry 5.8%. The day-ahead price cap was raised to 4,500 TL/MWh the same day.
